title: The Clever Octopus
summary: Octopuses can open jars, escape from tanks and recognise human faces. How can an animal so different from us be so smart?
paragraphs: In 2016, an octopus called Inky became famous around the world. He lived in a sea animal centre in New Zealand. One night, a worker forgot to close the top of his tank completely. Inky got out, moved across the floor and found a small pipe that led to the sea. When the workers arrived in the morning, he was gone. Only a wet path on the floor showed where he had escaped.

Stories like this are not unusual. These animals are among the cleverest in the sea. In experiments, they have learned to open glass containers with food inside, find their way through simple problems and use tools. Some collect half coconut shells from the sea floor, carry them around and use them as a home when they need to hide.

What makes them especially interesting is how different they are from us. Their closest relatives are snails, animals that are not known for their intelligence. Our last shared relative lived more than five hundred million years ago, and it was probably a very simple animal. This means that the octopus developed its intelligence in a completely different way from us and from birds.

An octopus has about five hundred million brain cells, a similar number to a dog. But only about one third of them are in its head. The rest are in its eight arms. Each arm can taste, touch and even make some simple decisions on its own. Scientists have seen an arm continue to reach for food while the animal was looking at something else.

They are also experts at hiding. Their skin contains thousands of special cells that can change colour in less than a second. Some can also change the surface of their skin to look like rocks or plants. One kind can even copy the shape and movements of other, more dangerous animals, such as sea snakes, to scare its enemies.

Many people who work with them believe that they have their own personalities. Some are shy, while others are curious and love to play. In one sea animal centre, an octopus did not like one particular worker. Every time she walked past its tank, it threw water at her. It did not do this to anyone else.

Sadly, most of them live for only one or two years. Some scientists wonder what they could achieve if they lived longer. As we learn more about these amazing animals, many people are also asking questions about how we should treat them.

questions.question: How did Inky escape from the sea animal centre?
options: A worker carried him to the sea
He got out of his tank and went down a pipe to the sea
He broke the glass of his tank
questions.explanation: He got out of the tank, crossed the floor and found a small pipe that led to the sea.

questions.question: What do some octopuses do with coconut shells?
options: They use them as a home to hide in
They use them to open containers
questions.explanation: They carry the shells around and use them as a home when they need to hide.

questions.question: Why is octopus intelligence especially interesting to scientists?
options: It developed in a completely different way from ours
questions.explanation: Octopuses developed intelligence separately; our last shared relative was a very simple animal.

questions.question: Where are most of an octopus's brain cells?
questions.explanation: Only about one third are in its head; the rest are in its eight arms.

questions.question: What does the story about the worker show?
options: Octopuses can recognise and react to individual people
Octopuses need a lot of water
questions.explanation: The octopus threw water only at one particular worker, which shows it recognised her.

grammar.structure: Present perfect for experiences and results
grammar.explanation: We use have/has + past participle for things that have happened at some time up to now, when the exact time is not important.
grammar.example: In experiments, they have learned to open glass containers with food inside, find their way through simple problems and use tools.

exercise.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Scientists have seen this many times.
Scientists have saw this many times.
Scientists has seen this many times.
Scientists seen have this many times.

grammar.explanation: While can join two contrasting ideas in one sentence.
grammar.example: Some are shy, while others are curious and love to play.

exercise.question: Choose the best word: Dogs live for many years, ___ octopuses live for only one or two.
exercise.explanation: The two ideas contrast, so we use while.
